preserved_constraints.text: 肝脏分割最新研究有哪些？

claims.text: 在本次检索到的证据中，可找到若干篇近期（2024–2026年检索窗口内）关于肝脏分割的摘要级研究，涵盖基于U-Net/FastAI、CNN-Transformer混合网络、细节增强多尺度融合网络以及3D深度卷积网络的方法；但所有证据均为摘要，未提供全文，且检索结果被截断，因此不能据此认为已覆盖该领域全部最新研究。
limitations: 检索返回结果被截断（truncated），不能代表全部文献

claims.text: 一项摘要报告提出基于U-Net深度学习架构并结合FastAI框架的肝脏图像分割方法，采用预处理与数据增强以改善泛化，并使用Dice相似系数和IoU作为评价指标；摘要称其相比传统分割技术取得更高的分割准确性和鲁棒性，但未给出具体数值。
limitations: 摘要未报告具体性能数值
未说明所用数据集细节

claims.text: 一项摘要提出WavPAC-Net，采用CNN-Transformer混合编码器（ConvNeXt-Small与Swin Transformer分支）、小波域融合模块和置换轴向-通道特征增强器，并在CirrMRI600+（T2加权MRI）上报告Dice 93.16%、IoU 88.45%、MCC 93.03%、计算复杂度19.88 GFLOPs，在LiTS CT数据集上报告Dice 96.91%、IoU 94.32%、MCC 96.79%。
limitations: 结果来自摘要，未经全文核验
不同数据集（MRI与CT）结果不可直接合并比较

claims.text: 该摘要称WavPAC-Net在与20个先进分割模型的系统比较中，在分割准确性和边界保真度上具有统计学显著优势；此为作者报告，摘要未提供比较细节或统计方法。
limitations: 比较细节与统计方法未在摘要中报告

claims.text: 一项摘要提出DEMF-Net，通过细节增强卷积（DE Conv）和多尺度特征融合模块（MSFF）改进肝脏特征学习，并在LiTS17数据集上报告各项评价指标有显著提升，但摘要未给出具体数值。
limitations: 摘要未报告具体指标数值

claims.text: 一项摘要提出基于3D深度卷积神经网络（3D-DCNN）的肝脏分割方法，结合中值/自适应滤波预处理、LBP与GLCM特征提取以及迭代区域生长（IRG），在腹部CT图像上评估，并称其优于Jaccard with JISTS-FCM、FCM和FCM-CSA等对比方法；摘要未报告具体数值。
limitations: 摘要未报告具体性能数值
对比方法的具体设置未说明

claims.text: 从这些摘要可归纳出近期肝脏分割研究的两条技术路线：一是以U-Net/CNN为基础并引入混合Transformer或小波融合以兼顾长程依赖与细节（如WavPAC-Net），二是通过细节增强与多尺度特征融合改进CNN（如DEMF-Net）；但各研究使用不同数据集（CirrMRI600+ MRI、LiTS CT、LiTS17）和不同评价指标，无法据此进行跨研究的性能汇总或优劣判定。
limitations: 数据集与指标不一致，不支持合并结果或优越性结论

openalex_record.title: Enhanced Liver Image Segmentation Using Custom Metric and Unet with FastAI
openalex_record.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology
openalex_record.abstract: Liver segmentation from medical images is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis for detecting liver abnormalities and supporting clinical decision-making. However, accurate segmentation remains challenging due to variations in liver shape, intensity, and the presence of surrounding organs. In this paper, an enhanced liver image segmentation approach is proposed using the U-Net deep learning architecture implemented with the FastAI framework. The proposed method utilizes efficient preprocessing techniques and data augmentation to improve model generalization. In addition, custom evaluation metrics, including the Dice Similarity Coefficient and Intersection over Union (IoU), are incorporated to better measure segmentation performance and optimize the training process. The model is trained and validated on liver medical image datasets to accurately identify and segment liver regions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves improved segmentation accuracy and robustness compared to conventional segmentation techniques. The integration of FastAI with U-Net simplifies model development while maintaining high performance, making the proposed method suitable for real- time clinical support and automated medical image analysis.

sources.title: Enhanced Liver Image Segmentation Using Custom Metric and Unet with FastAI
sources.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology

evidence.text: Liver segmentation from medical images is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis for detecting liver abnormalities and supporting clinical decision-making. However, accurate segmentation remains challenging due to variations in liver shape, intensity, and the presence of surrounding organs. In this paper, an enhanced liver image segmentation approach is proposed using the U-Net deep learning architecture implemented with the FastAI framework. The proposed method utilizes efficient preprocessing techniques and data augmentation to improve model generalization. In addition, custom evaluation metrics, including the Dice Similarity Coefficient and Intersection over Union (IoU), are incorporated to better measure segmentation performance and optimize the training process. The model is trained and validated on liver medical image datasets to accurately identify and segment liver regions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves improved segmentation accuracy and robustness compared to conventional segmentation techniques. The integration of FastAI with U-Net simplifies model development while maintaining high performance, making the proposed method suitable for real- time clinical support and automated medical image analysis.

openalex_record.title: WavPAC-Net: a wavelet-based hybrid encoder network with permuted axial-channel feature enhancement for liver segmentation
openalex_record.journal: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
openalex_record.abstract: The liver, core to human metabolism and detoxification, is threatened by chronic diseases like cirrhosis that increase hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk, with early diagnosis dependent on accurate liver segmentation in medical imaging. Current clinical segmentation methods generally suffer from low efficiency, strong subjectivity, and scarcity of AI-driven commercial products. Although deep learning technologies have been applied to liver segmentation, mainstream architectures still exhibit inherent limitations: CNN struggles with long-range dependencies while Transformer lacks fine detail representation. This study proposes WavPAC-Net, an innovative wavelet-based fusion network incorporating: (1) a hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder combining ConvNeXt-Small branch for precise hepatic parenchymal texture capture and Swin Transformer branch for long-range dependency modeling; (2) a Wavelet Domain Fusion Module (WDFM) that decomposes the features extracted by CNN and Transformer into low-frequency and high-frequency sub-bands respectively, and performs adaptive weighted fusion; and (3) a Permuted Axial-Channel Feature Enhancer (PACFE) that implements cross-dimensional refinement of high-dimensional fused features through collaborative three-dimensional spatial modeling and channel dimension permutation. In systematic comparisons with 20 state-of-the-art segmentation models, WavPAC-Net demonstrates statistically significant advantages in both segmentation accuracy and boundary fidelity. Evaluated on the CirrMRI600+ dataset (T2-weighted MRI), WavPAC-Net achieved Dice score of 93.16%, IoU of 88.45%, and MCC of 93.03%, with a computational complexity of 19.88 GFLOPs. Multi-modal validation on the public LiTS CT dataset further confirmed the model’s excellent performance, achieving Dice score of 96.91%, IoU of 94.32%, and MCC of 96.79%. Overall, WavPAC-Net provides an effective balance between segmentation accuracy and computational complexity, supporting its potential for practical liver segmentation applications.

sources.title: WavPAC-Net: a wavelet-based hybrid encoder network with permuted axial-channel feature enhancement for liver segmentation
sources.journal: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences

evidence.text: The liver, core to human metabolism and detoxification, is threatened by chronic diseases like cirrhosis that increase hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk, with early diagnosis dependent on accurate liver segmentation in medical imaging. Current clinical segmentation methods generally suffer from low efficiency, strong subjectivity, and scarcity of AI-driven commercial products. Although deep learning technologies have been applied to liver segmentation, mainstream architectures still exhibit inherent limitations: CNN struggles with long-range dependencies while Transformer lacks fine detail representation. This study proposes WavPAC-Net, an innovative wavelet-based fusion network incorporating: (1) a hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder combining ConvNeXt-Small branch for precise hepatic parenchymal texture capture and Swin Transformer branch for long-range dependency modeling; (2) a Wavelet Domain Fusion Module (WDFM) that decomposes the features extracted by CNN and Transformer into low-frequency and high-frequency sub-bands respectively, and performs adaptive weighted fusion; and (3) a Permuted Axial-Channel Feature Enhancer (PACFE) that implements cross-dimensional refinement of high-dimensional fused features through collaborative three-dimensional spatial modeling and channel dimension permutation. In systematic comparisons with 20 state-of-the-art segmentation models, WavPAC-Net demonstrates statistically significant advantages in both segmentation accuracy and boundary fidelity. Evaluated on the CirrMRI600+ dataset (T2-weighted MRI), WavPAC-Net achieved Dice score of 93.16%, IoU of 88.45%, and MCC of 93.03%, with a computational complexity of 19.88 GFLOPs. Multi-modal validation on the public LiTS CT dataset further confirmed the model’s excellent performance, achieving Dice score of 96.91%, IoU of 94.32%, and MCC of 96.79%. Overall, WavPAC-Net provides an effective balance between segmentation accuracy and computational complexity, supporting its potential for practical liver segmentation applications.

openalex_record.title: Liver segmentation network based on detail enhancement and multi-scale feature fusion
openalex_record.abstract: Due to the low contrast of abdominal CT (Computer Tomography) images and the similar color and shape of the liver to other organs such as the spleen, stomach, and kidneys, liver segmentation presents significant challenges. Additionally, 2D CT images obtained from different angles (such as sagittal, coronal, and transverse planes) increase the diversity of liver morphology and the complexity of segmentation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Detail Enhanced Convolution (DE Conv) to improve liver feature learning and thereby enhance liver segmentation performance. Furthermore, to enable the model to better learn liver features at different scales, a Multi-Scale Feature Fusion module (MSFF) is added to the skip connections in the model. The MSFF module enhances the capture of global features, thus improving the accuracy of the liver segmentation model. Through the aforementioned research, this paper proposes a liver segmentation network based on detail enhancement and multi-scale feature fusion (DEMF-Net). We conducted extensive experiments on the LiTS17 dataset, and the results demonstrate that the DEMF-Net model achieved significant improvements across various evaluation metrics. Therefore, the proposed DEMF-Net model can achieve precise liver segmentation.

sources.title: Liver segmentation network based on detail enhancement and multi-scale feature fusion

evidence.text: Due to the low contrast of abdominal CT (Computer Tomography) images and the similar color and shape of the liver to other organs such as the spleen, stomach, and kidneys, liver segmentation presents significant challenges. Additionally, 2D CT images obtained from different angles (such as sagittal, coronal, and transverse planes) increase the diversity of liver morphology and the complexity of segmentation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Detail Enhanced Convolution (DE Conv) to improve liver feature learning and thereby enhance liver segmentation performance. Furthermore, to enable the model to better learn liver features at different scales, a Multi-Scale Feature Fusion module (MSFF) is added to the skip connections in the model. The MSFF module enhances the capture of global features, thus improving the accuracy of the liver segmentation model. Through the aforementioned research, this paper proposes a liver segmentation network based on detail enhancement and multi-scale feature fusion (DEMF-Net). We conducted extensive experiments on the LiTS17 dataset, and the results demonstrate that the DEMF-Net model achieved significant improvements across various evaluation metrics. Therefore, the proposed DEMF-Net model can achieve precise liver segmentation.

openalex_record.title: Efficient Liver Segmentation using Advanced 3D-DCNN Algorithm on CT Images
openalex_record.abstract: According to the latest global cancer statistics for 2022, liver cancer ranks as the ninth most common disease in women. Segmenting the liver and distinguishing it from tumors within it pose a significant challenge due to the complex nature of liver imaging. Common imaging methods such as Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Computer Tomography (CT), and Ultrasound (US) are employed to distinguish liver tissue from liver tumors after collecting a sample. Attempting to partition the liver and tumor based on grayscale shades or shapes in abdominal CT images is not ideal because of the overlapping intensity levels and the variability in the location and shape of soft tissues. To address this issue, this study introduces an effective method for liver image segmentation using a 3D deep Convolutional Neural Network (3D-DCNN). The process involves several stages. First, liver images undergo preprocessing to enhance image quality, including median filtering, adaptive filtering, and converting them to grayscale. The feature extraction phase focuses on extracting four sets of features, such as the Local Binary Pattern (LBP) and the Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM). Additionally, an Iterative Region Growing (IRG) technique is developed to improve the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) prediction by enhancing the quality of the input images obtained from segmented images. This method enables the segmentation of the liver in abdominal CT image volumes and can subsequently be used to segment liver tumor images to evaluate the performance of the proposed 3D-DLNN approach. This method was implemented in MATLAB, and its performance was evaluated using various metrics. In experimental analysis, the proposed technique outperformed other methods, including Jaccard with JISTS-FCM, Fuzzy C-Means (FCM), and FCM with Cluster Size Adjustment (FCM-CSA).

Segmenting the liver and distinguishing it from tumors within it pose a significant challenge due to the complex nature of liver imaging. Common imaging methods such as Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Computer Tomography (CT), and Ultrasound (US) are employed to distinguish liver tissue from liver tumors after collecting a sample. Attempting to partition the liver and tumor based on grayscale shades or shapes in abdominal CT images is not ideal because of the overlapping intensity levels and the variability in the location and shape of soft tissues. To address this issue, this study introduces an effective method for liver image segmentation using a 3D deep Convolutional Neural Network (3D-DCNN). The process involves several stages. First, liver images undergo preprocessing to enhance image quality, including median filtering, adaptive filtering, and converting them to grayscale. The feature extraction phase focuses on extracting four sets of features, such as the Local Binary Pattern (LBP) and the Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM). Additionally, an Iterative Region Growing (IRG) technique is developed to improve the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) prediction by enhancing the quality of the input images obtained from segmented images. This method enables the segmentation of the liver in abdominal CT image volumes and can subsequently be used to segment liver tumor images to evaluate the performance of the proposed 3D-DLNN approach. This method was implemented in MATLAB, and its performance was evaluated using various metrics. In experimental analysis, the proposed technique outperformed other methods, including Jaccard with JISTS-FCM, Fuzzy C-Means (FCM), and FCM with Cluster Size Adjustment (FCM-CSA).

records.title: Automated liver segmentation from CT images using modified ResUNet
records.abstract: The Segmentation of liver from computed tomography (CT) images is a critical task in medical research particularly when employing deep learning methods. Most doctors prefer to use Computed tomography images for liver disease identification hence automatic liver segmentation plays a decisive role. To perform automatic segmentation of liver popular architectures such as modified ResUNet are specifically designed to capture multi-resolution features. In this study we proposed an automatic system that utilizes convolutional layers to efficiently extract features while maintaining spatial information. A modified Residual UNet model was developed for liver segmentation using the 3Dircadb dataset, the model demonstrated excellent performance by achieving a Dice Score of 93.08% , accuracy of 98.57%, Jaccard Index of 87.12%, a volumetric overlap error of 12.87 % , and a relative volume difference of 14.91% on 128x128 size images. These results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed method. The primary goal of this research is to apply deep learning techniques for liver segmentation and assess the model’s performance using segmentation metrics.

records.title: Explainable and Robust Deep Learning for Liver Segmentation Through U-Net Network
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Clinical imaging techniques, such as magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography, play a vital role in supporting clinicians by aiding disease diagnosis and facilitating the planning of appropriate interventions. This is particularly important in malignant conditions like hepatocellular carcinoma, where accurate image segmentation, delineating the liver and tumor, is a critical initial step in optimizing diagnosis, staging, and treatment planning, including interventions like transplantation, surgical resection, radiotherapy, portal vein embolization, and other procedures. Therefore, effective segmentation methods can significantly influence both diagnostic accuracy and treatment outcomes. Method: In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based approach aimed at accurately segmenting the liver in medical images, thus addressing a critical need in hepatic disease diagnosis and treatment planning. We consider a U-Net architecture with residual connections to capture fine-grained anatomical details. We also take into account the prediction explainability, aiming to highlight, in the image under analysis, the areas that are symptomatic for a certain segmentation. In detail, by exploiting the U-Net architecture, two different models are trained with two annotated datasets of computed tomography medical images, resulting in four different experiments. Results: We consider two different datasets to improve robustness and generalization across diverse patient populations and imaging conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method obtains interesting performances, with an accuracy ranging from 0.81 to 0.93. Conclusions: We thus show that the proposed method can provide a reliable and efficient solution for automated liver segmentation, promising significant advancements in clinical workflows and precision medicine.

records.title: A Reverse Mamba Attention Network for Pathological Liver Segmentation
records.journal: International Conference on Electrical, Computer, Communications and Mechatronics Engineering (ICECCME)
records.abstract: We present RMA-Mamba, a novel architecture that advances the capabilities of vision state space models through a specialized reverse mamba attention module (RMA). The key innovation lies in RMA-Mamba’s ability to capture long-range dependencies while maintaining precise local feature representation through its hierarchical processing pipeline. By integrating Vision Mamba (VMamba)’s efficient sequence modeling with RMA’s targeted feature refinement, our architecture achieves superior feature learning across multiple scales. This dualmechanism approach enables robust handling of complex morphological patterns while maintaining computational efficiency. We demonstrate RMA-Mamba’s effectiveness in the challenging domain of pathological liver segmentation (from both CT and MRI), where traditional segmentation approaches often fail due to tissue variations. When evaluated on a newly introduced cirrhotic liver dataset (CirrMRI600+) of T2-weighted MRI scans, RMA-Mamba achieves the state-of-the-art performance with a Dice coefficient of $92.08 \%$, mean IoU of $87.36 \%$, and recall of $\mathbf{9 2. 9 6 \%}$. The architecture’s generalizability is further validated on the cancerous liver segmentation from CT scans (LiTS: Liver Tumor Segmentation dataset), yielding a Dice score of 92.9% and $\mathbf{m I o U}$ of $\mathbf{8 8. 9 9 \%}$. The source code of the proposed RMA-Mamba is available after double blind review. Our code is available for public: https://github.com/JunZengz/RMAMamba.

records.title: Liver segmentation algorithm based on improved UNet
records.journal: International Conference on Biomedicine and Bioinformatics Engineering (ICBBE)
records.abstract: This paper proposes an improved UNet architecture (RR UNet) for liver segmentation in CT images. To address the problems of irregular liver shape and blurred boundary, the Recurrent Attention Block(RABlock) module is introduced into the decoder to enhance the feature expression ability and boundary recognition accuracy. At the same time, the Residual Skip Connection (RSC) module is used to promote multi-scale semantic information fusion, and the hybrid loss function of BCE and Focal Loss is combined to alleviate the class imbalance problem. The experimental results on the LiTS2017 dataset show that RR UNet significantly improves multiple performance indicators compared to the baseline model: mIoU reaches 95.8%, DSC rises to 87.7%, Precision is 98.6%, Recall reaches 97.1%, and ASSD drops to 3.48mm. This method effectively improves the accuracy and robustness of liver segmentation.

records.title: Liver segmentation network based on detail enhancement and multi-scale feature fusion
records.abstract: Due to the low contrast of abdominal CT (Computer Tomography) images and the similar color and shape of the liver to other organs such as the spleen, stomach, and kidneys, liver segmentation presents significant challenges. Additionally, 2D CT images obtained from different angles (such as sagittal, coronal, and transverse planes) increase the diversity of liver morphology and the complexity of segmentation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Detail Enhanced Convolution (DE Conv) to improve liver feature learning and thereby enhance liver segmentation performance. Furthermore, to enable the model to better learn liver features at different scales, a Multi-Scale Feature Fusion module (MSFF) is added to the skip connections in the model. The MSFF module enhances the capture of global features, thus improving the accuracy of the liver segmentation model. Through the aforementioned research, this paper proposes a liver segmentation network based on detail enhancement and multi-scale feature fusion (DEMF-Net). We conducted extensive experiments on the LiTS17 dataset, and the results demonstrate that the DEMF-Net model achieved significant improvements across various evaluation metrics. Therefore, the proposed DEMF-Net model can achieve precise liver segmentation.

records.title: Clinical Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Chronic Hepatitis B
records.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) burdens the healthcare system, affecting millions of individuals worldwide with a potential progression to complications such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The World Health Organization launched the chronic viral hepatitis elimination plan which aimed to eliminate chronic hepatitis B virus by 2030, yet the goal has seemed to be far from reach with the remaining few years owing to different hurdles ranging from screening strategy and diagnosis to risk stratification for antiviral treatment and HCC surveillance. To refine the management of CHB, previous studies focused on identifying the at-risk populations and predictors for adverse outcomes using conventional statistical methods. With the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI), there is further room to improve different aspects of screening and management. For instance, generative AI, such as large language models (LLMs), has been proven to have the ability to answer different clinical questions, assisting patients' and physicians' decision on various clinical scenarios. Different machine learning and deep learning models have also been developed to assess for liver fibrosis, as well as to aid segmentation of liver structures and detection of focal liver lesions through various imaging modalities. While different AI models have shown superior performance compared to those developed through traditional statistical models, the lack of standardized datasets in training cohorts and the unresolved concerns of hallucination of false information in LLMs pose challenges on applying AI in the current management of CHB, in which further studies are required to adopt AI into daily clinical practice.

records.title: Quantized TotalSegmentator for Fast Abdominal Organ Segmentation on CPUs
records.abstract: BACKGROUND. TotalSegmentator is designed for a graphics processing unit (GPU), runs slowly on a central processing unit (CPU), and depends on Python, limiting CPU-only clinical deployment. OBJECTIVE. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether TS-Portable, a self-contained CPU executable running 8-bit integer (INT8)–quantized TotalSegmentator models, is noninferior to the reference implementation across 15 abdominal organs in an external multicenter cohort, quantify CPU-only runtime, and demonstrate spleen volumetry on a picture archiving and communication system (PACS) reading station. METHODS. This retrospective study compared TS-Portable with the reference Python implementation on 100 external multicenter CT scans and 28 chronic liver disease series. Per-case mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and 3-mm normalized surface distance (NSD@3 mm) across 15 organs (1.5-mm resolution) and spleen-only mode were tested against a 0.01 noninferiority margin (paired bootstrap 95% CIs). Workstation and PACS runtimes were recorded; spleen volumes were compared via Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTS. The external cohort included 100 patients (53 men, 47 women; mean age, 53 ± 16 [SD] years). Across 15 organs, TS-Portable was noninferior for mean DSC (difference, 0.00017; 95% CI, 0.00003 to 0.00031; p < .001) and NSD@3 mm (difference, 0.00015; 95% CI, −0.00002 to 0.00031; p < .001) and in spleen-only mode (both p < .001). Workstation 1.5-mm median runtime was 48.0 seconds for TS-Portable on CPU versus 342.5 seconds on CPU (ratio, 7.14) and 61.5 seconds on GPU (ratio, 1.28) for the reference. On PACS, CPU spleen volumetry took 5.8 versus 43.4 seconds, agreeing with the reference (CCC, 0.9999; bias, 0.2%; 95% limits of agreement, −7.2% to 7.6%) and manual contours (CCC, 0.989; bias, −6.8%). In 28 chronic liver disease series, TS-Portable ran from DICOM in 6.5 seconds (median), agreeing with the reference (CCC, 0.99999) and manual contours (CCC, 0.992; bias, −3.4%). CONCLUSION. TS-Portable achieved noninferior abdominal organ segmentation accuracy compared with the reference implementation while running faster on a workstation CPU than the reference on a GPU. CLINICAL IMPACT. Self-contained deployment enables fast multiorgan segmentation on CPU-only computers and spleen volumetry within seconds on a standard reading station, without dedicated GPUs or software installation.

records.title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
records.abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings. Liver ultrasound is operator-dependent. Here, the authors develop a lightweight, patient-mounted robot for autonomous liver scanning in clinical, remote and mobile settings, with results comparable to those gathered by experienced sonographers.

records.title: WavPAC-Net: a wavelet-based hybrid encoder network with permuted axial-channel feature enhancement for liver segmentation
records.journal: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
records.abstract: The liver, core to human metabolism and detoxification, is threatened by chronic diseases like cirrhosis that increase hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk, with early diagnosis dependent on accurate liver segmentation in medical imaging. Current clinical segmentation methods generally suffer from low efficiency, strong subjectivity, and scarcity of AI-driven commercial products. Although deep learning technologies have been applied to liver segmentation, mainstream architectures still exhibit inherent limitations: CNN struggles with long-range dependencies while Transformer lacks fine detail representation. This study proposes WavPAC-Net, an innovative wavelet-based fusion network incorporating: (1) a hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder combining ConvNeXt-Small branch for precise hepatic parenchymal texture capture and Swin Transformer branch for long-range dependency modeling; (2) a Wavelet Domain Fusion Module (WDFM) that decomposes the features extracted by CNN and Transformer into low-frequency and high-frequency sub-bands respectively, and performs adaptive weighted fusion; and (3) a Permuted Axial-Channel Feature Enhancer (PACFE) that implements cross-dimensional refinement of high-dimensional fused features through collaborative three-dimensional spatial modeling and channel dimension permutation. In systematic comparisons with 20 state-of-the-art segmentation models, WavPAC-Net demonstrates statistically significant advantages in both segmentation accuracy and boundary fidelity. Evaluated on the CirrMRI600+ dataset (T2-weighted MRI), WavPAC-Net achieved Dice score of 93.16%, IoU of 88.45%, and MCC of 93.03%, with a computational complexity of 19.88 GFLOPs. Multi-modal validation on the public LiTS CT dataset further confirmed the model’s excellent performance, achieving Dice score of 96.91%, IoU of 94.32%, and MCC of 96.79%. Overall, WavPAC-Net provides an effective balance between segmentation accuracy and computational complexity, supporting its potential for practical liver segmentation applications.

records.title: LIVER CANCER DETECTION USING RESNET, SWIN TRANSFORMER AND CONVNEXT TINY NETWORKS
records.journal: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
records.abstract: Liver tumor detection from CT images is challenging because most CT slices do not contain tumors, while only a small number contain tumor regions. Another challenge is that slices from the same patient can be very similar, which may cause data leakage when splitting the data randomly. This study focuses on classifying liver CT slices into Tumor and No-Tumor classes using deep learning. The LiTS and 3Dircadb datasets are combined and used for the experiments. Three deep learning models, Swin-T, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and ResNet-50, are trained and evaluated. A patient-level data split is used to keep patients in the training, validation, and test sets separate. The three models are also combined using a soft-voting ensemble. The final evaluation is performed on an unseen test set containing 6,323 slices. The soft-voting ensemble achieved the highest accuracy of 92.74%. These results show that the models can detect tumor and no-tumor slices, while the class imbalance remains an important challenge for tumor detection.

records.title: The applications of artificial intelligence in liver transplantation: A comprehensive scoping review
records.abstract: Liver transplantation (LT) is a complex surgical intervention, with intricate decision-making and risks at all stages before, during and after the procedure itself. Artificial intelligence (AI) may assist the process but has seen limited use. This scoping review assessed primary articles reporting on clinical AI in LT in MEDLINE and Embase from 2000 to September 2026. 196 articles were identified: focusing on the pre-operative period before transplant (21.9%), organ retrieval (9.7%), intra-operative issues (3.6%), short-term post-operative complications (16.8%), long-term post-operative complications (45.9%) and natural language processing (2.0%). 95.9% had retrospective designs and only 12.8% had direct multi-centre data, with the rest from national registries or single centres. 13.8% of studies externally validated their AI tools. Only one study performed a prospective evaluation of their tool with a randomized controlled trial. Progress towards clinically deployable tools will require harmonised, higher-granularity datasets, consistent reporting, and prospective evaluation within real-world transplant workflows.

records.title: A multiparametric liver MRI dataset with multiple tumor and liver segmentations of pre-treatment hepatocellular carcinomas
records.abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver cancer and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. While dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) plays a key role for HCC screening, diagnosis and treatment planning, the development of AI models for detection and characterization of focal liver lesions is hindered by the scarcity of publicly available annotated MRI datasets. Here, we present OpenSwissHCC, a curated multiphasic dataset of 132 multiparametric DCE-MRI scans from adult patients with chronic liver disease acquired on 1.5 T and 3 T MRI scanners between 2011 and 2020. The dataset includes both HCC-positive (n = 63) and HCC-negative (n = 69) patients, with up to five lesions per patient segmented across each sequence when confidently identified. Whole-liver and lesion segmentations were manually performed and expert-validated, with lesion metadata including LI-RADS scores, size, liver segment location, major LI-RADS imaging features (non-rim APHE, washout, capsule, threshold growth) and key ancillary/background findings (e.g., mosaic architecture, fat/blood products, necrosis, tumor-in-vein; cirrhosis and portal-hypertension signs). In total, 140 lesions were annotated, including 97 confirmed HCC. Additionally, we provide liver masks for all T1-weighted images (T1-WI) sequences, generated using a pre-trained nnU-Net model, as well as pre-computed transforms to facilitate registration across T1-WI phases. By providing a comprehensive, well-annotated, and standardized collection of liver MRI examinations, OpenSwissHCC aims to assist the development and benchmarking of advanced computational methods for automated HCC detection, segmentation, and characterization, fostering progress toward precision imaging and personalized treatment planning.

records.title: Segment anything model (SAM)‐driven prompt‐guided interactive delineation of gross tumor volume for rectal cancer neoadjuvant radiotherapy
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Segment Anything Model (SAM), a prompt-guided foundation model, exhibits substantial potential for medical image segmentation by incorporating prior knowledge through user-defined prompts. However, the application of SAM in radiotherapy target delineation remains limited. PURPOSE: This study proposes a feasible prompt-guided interactive delineation workflow driven by an optimized SAM. METHODS: A total of 100 rectal cancer neoadjuvant radiotherapy cases were collected (60 for training and 40 for testing). This study utilized bounding-box prompts to guide SAM for GTV segmentation. Physicians manually draw box prompts on certain slices, while box prompts for the remaining slices are automatically generated using an interpolation strategy. Four fine-tuning strategies for SAM training were evaluated, and the impact of prompt numbers and placements was assessed as well. The performance of the finalized workflow with optimized SAM was compared with five state-of-the-art (SOTA) models, and its robustness to prompt variations in middle-slice selection and box-prompt margins was analyzed. RESULTS: Compared to other fine-tuning methods, freezing the image encoder obtained the most stable performance. Prompts on only 3 slices achieved accuracy comparable to prompts on all slices. The placement of the middle-slice prompt exhibited negligible impact (p > 0.05). The finalized SAM-driven workflow outperformed end-to-end baseline models both visually and quantitatively (3D DSC: 0.92 vs 0.80; 3D HD95: 2.73 vs 12.70; IoU: 0.86 vs 0.67; Sensitivity: 91.20% vs 85.98%; Precision: 93.65% vs 79.23%), while maintaining stable performance across certain prompt variations. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed SAM-driven interactive workflow with as few as 3 box prompts achieves favorable accuracy of GTV segmentation for rectal cancer neoadjuvant radiotherapy.

records.title: Enhanced Liver Image Segmentation Using Custom Metric and Unet with FastAI
records.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: Liver segmentation from medical images is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis for detecting liver abnormalities and supporting clinical decision-making. However, accurate segmentation remains challenging due to variations in liver shape, intensity, and the presence of surrounding organs. In this paper, an enhanced liver image segmentation approach is proposed using the U-Net deep learning architecture implemented with the FastAI framework. The proposed method utilizes efficient preprocessing techniques and data augmentation to improve model generalization. In addition, custom evaluation metrics, including the Dice Similarity Coefficient and Intersection over Union (IoU), are incorporated to better measure segmentation performance and optimize the training process. The model is trained and validated on liver medical image datasets to accurately identify and segment liver regions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves improved segmentation accuracy and robustness compared to conventional segmentation techniques. The integration of FastAI with U-Net simplifies model development while maintaining high performance, making the proposed method suitable for real- time clinical support and automated medical image analysis.

records.title: MF‐ResUnet: A 3D Liver Image Segmentation Method Based on Multi‐Scale Feature Fusion
records.journal: International Journal of Medical Robotics and Computer Assisted Surgery
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Due to the variable shapes of the liver parenchyma, minimal voxel intensity differences with adjacent organs, and discontinuous liver boundaries, automatic liver segmentation from computerised tomography images poses significant challenges. METHODS: In this study, we propose a 3D liver segmentation method based on multiscale feature fusion. This network employs SE channel attention to recalibrate liver features. Additionally, it utilises an AMF module for multiscale feature fusion to obtain rich spatial information. Furthermore, we introduce the NGAB module to address the deteriorating effects of dilated convolutions as the dilation rate increases, contributing to enhanced feature representation and improving accuracy in liver segmentation. RESULTS: Experimental results on the publicly available LiTS2017 dataset and 3DIRCADb dataset show that our proposed framework achieves a DSC of 0.977 and 0.967 in liver segmentation, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed method can adequately capture multiscale characteristics, showing promising prospects for automatic liver segmentation.

records.title: Enhanced Liver Image Segmentation Using Custom Metric and Unet with FastAI
records.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology
records.abstract: Liver segmentation from medical images is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis for detecting liver abnormalities and supporting clinical decision-making. However, accurate segmentation remains challenging due to variations in liver shape, intensity, and the presence of surrounding organs. In this paper, an enhanced liver image segmentation approach is proposed using the U-Net deep learning architecture implemented with the FastAI framework. The proposed method utilizes efficient preprocessing techniques and data augmentation to improve model generalization. In addition, custom evaluation metrics, including the Dice Similarity Coefficient and Intersection over Union (IoU), are incorporated to better measure segmentation performance and optimize the training process. The model is trained and validated on liver medical image datasets to accurately identify and segment liver regions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves improved segmentation accuracy and robustness compared to conventional segmentation techniques. The integration of FastAI with U-Net simplifies model development while maintaining high performance, making the proposed method suitable for real- time clinical support and automated medical image analysis.

records.title: MRI Liver Image Segmentation Based on Cascade Transformer and U-Net
authors: ZHANG  Tiansen, XU  Xiaona, ZHAO  Yue, ZHANG  Xinning
records.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
records.abstract: Achieving accurate Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) liver image segmentation is of great significance in the field of medicine. It assists doctors in rapidly locating a target region, aids treatment, and plays a key role in postoperative observation. However, MRI images contain rich semantic information and numerous abnormal noises. Traditional convolutional operations have certain limitations in image processing, with limited global modeling capability, limited receptive fields, and difficulty in capturing global information. Moreover, the hierarchy of convolution-based networks should not be too deep because deep networks tend to increase the number of parameters and miss important semantic information at high resolutions. To address these problems, this study introduces the application of Transformers in image processing to establish global information associations, to better capture global information and achieve accurate target location. However, the Transformer may destroy local details when processing detailed image features and performs poorly in providing inductive bias. To leverage the advantages of the Transformer and convolution, this study proposes a feature modeling method that works in cascade. First, coarse segmentation of the Region of Interest (RoI) is achieved by using the Medical Transformer (MedT) network, which uses fewer parameters and requires less computational effort, as the upstream network. Then, the extracted RoI region is data processed and fed into a downstream U-Net network for secondary segmentation, where special attention is paid to local information during the second segmentation to obtain finer prediction results. Experiments on the CHAOS dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant results in liver segmentation tasks, with a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.922 and an Intersection over Union (IoU) score of 0.877.

records.title: Combination of Image Enhancement and Double U-Net Architecture for Liver Segmentation in CT-Scan Images
records.journal: Journal of Electronics Electromedical Engineering and Medical Informatics
records.abstract: Liver cancer can be identified using CT-Scan liver image segmentation. Liver segmentation can be performed using CNN architecture like U-Net. However, the segmentation results using U-Net architecture are affected by image quality. Low image quality can affect the accuracy of segmentation results. This study proposes a combination of image enhancement and segmentation stages on CT-Scan liver images. Image enhancement is achieved by using a combination of CLAHE to enhance contrast and Bilateral Filter to reduce noise. The segmentation architecture proposed in this study is Double U-Net which is a development of U-Net architecture by adding a second U-Net block with the same structure as a single U-Net. The first U-Net is used to extract simple features, while the second U-Net is used to extract more complex features and enhance the segmentation results of the first U-Net. PSNR and SSIM measure the results of image enhancement. The PSNR is more than 40dB and the SSIM result is close to 1. These results show that the proposed image enhancement method can enhance the quality of original images. The segmentation results were measured by calculating accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, dice score, and IoU. The result of liver segmentation obtained 99% for accuracy, 98% for sensitivity, 99% for specificity, 98% for dice score, and 90% for IoU. This shows that liver segmentation using Double U-Net obtained good segmentation. Results of image enhancement and image segmentation show that the proposed method is very good for enhancing image quality and performing liver segmentation accurately.

records.title: Efficient Liver Segmentation using Advanced 3D-DCNN Algorithm on CT Images
records.abstract: According to the latest global cancer statistics for 2022, liver cancer ranks as the ninth most common disease in women. Segmenting the liver and distinguishing it from tumors within it pose a significant challenge due to the complex nature of liver imaging. Common imaging methods such as Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Computer Tomography (CT), and Ultrasound (US) are employed to distinguish liver tissue from liver tumors after collecting a sample. Attempting to partition the liver and tumor based on grayscale shades or shapes in abdominal CT images is not ideal because of the overlapping intensity levels and the variability in the location and shape of soft tissues. To address this issue, this study introduces an effective method for liver image segmentation using a 3D deep Convolutional Neural Network (3D-DCNN). The process involves several stages. First, liver images undergo preprocessing to enhance image quality, including median filtering, adaptive filtering, and converting them to grayscale. The feature extraction phase focuses on extracting four sets of features, such as the Local Binary Pattern (LBP) and the Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM). Additionally, an Iterative Region Growing (IRG) technique is developed to improve the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) prediction by enhancing the quality of the input images obtained from segmented images. This method enables the segmentation of the liver in abdominal CT image volumes and can subsequently be used to segment liver tumor images to evaluate the performance of the proposed 3D-DLNN approach. This method was implemented in MATLAB, and its performance was evaluated using various metrics. In experimental analysis, the proposed technique outperformed other methods, including Jaccard with JISTS-FCM, Fuzzy C-Means (FCM), and FCM with Cluster Size Adjustment (FCM-CSA).

records.title: U-Net++ architecture: A nested and dense design for multi-scale liver image segmentation from 2D CT scans
records.abstract: The mission of segmenting medical images is to split up an image into various areas based on some predefined criteria, which is essential. Convolutional neural networks have always been important and effective for segmentation tasks, especially for medical images, and the U-Net architecture is one of the most popular alternatives. In U-Net++, each pathway has a variety of depths and resolutions, allowing it to capture multiscale contextual information from the final image. The pathways are connected in a nested fashion, each receiving information from the first one, permitting us to more concluded segmentation of objects at different scales. To enhance the efficiency of U-Net++ for real-world and useful applications, we also introduce deep supervision during training. This allows for the lowering of redundant pathways at inference time without any problem in accuracy, reducing the computational complexity of the model. For validating our developed model we used the 3DIRCADB dataset for the liver segmentation from 2D abdominal Computed tomography scans and achieved good results. In gist, U-Net++ is an amazing power source architecture for image segmentation tasks, giving and suggesting a dense design that can capture multi-scale contextual information and preserve spatial information. It tells residual and skip connections to lower the vanishing gradient problem and deep supervision to improve efficiency.

records.abstract: The liver is the biggest gland and largest internal organ.Thus, it performs dual roles in the human body.It is a vital and unique organ without which the tissues of the body speedily perish from deficiency in vitality and nutrients.At the same time, the liver has a limited ability to regenerate dead or damaged tissues.Hence, no mechanism or medicine can compensate for the loss of liver functions.It is a reddish-brown organ with lobes of irregular size and shape.The liver's size is dependent on numerous factors: age, gender, body size, weight, and health conditions [1].
